description: Prepositions question bank generated from FDA & SDA Competitive Examination Notes (General English — 17.5 Prepositions). Covers definition, types, time, place, position, direction, movement, manner, means, agent, cause, phrase prepositions, fixed combinations after verbs/adjectives/nouns, contrasts, common errors, revision tables and practice questions. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a preposition?

options.A: A word that shows the relationship of a noun, pronoun or noun phrase to another word in a sentence
options.B: A word that describes an action or state
options.C: A word that modifies a verb, adjective or another adverb
options.D: A word that joins two clauses

questions.explanation: A preposition shows the relationship of a noun, pronoun or noun phrase to another word in a sentence, e.g. 'The book is on the table.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does a preposition usually indicate?

options.B: Time, place, position, direction, movement, manner, means, cause, agent, possession or other relationships

questions.explanation: A preposition usually indicates time, place, position, direction, movement, manner, means, cause, agent, possession or other relationships.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the object of a preposition?

options.A: The verb governed by the preposition
options.B: The noun, pronoun or noun phrase governed by the preposition
options.C: The adjective modified by the preposition

questions.explanation: The object of a preposition is the noun, pronoun or noun phrase governed by the preposition. In 'She sat beside Ravi,' Ravi is the object of beside.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a prepositional phrase?

options.A: A preposition together with its object and any modifiers
options.B: A phrase that contains only a preposition
options.C: A clause beginning with a conjunction
options.D: A phrase that functions as a verb

questions.explanation: A prepositional phrase is a preposition together with its object and any modifiers, e.g. 'under the old bridge,' 'at the station,' 'because of heavy rain.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Can a preposition be followed by a pronoun?

options.B: Yes, but the pronoun normally takes the object form
options.C: Yes, but only in formal writing
options.D: Only if the pronoun is possessive

questions.explanation: Yes, but the pronoun normally takes the object form: 'between you and me,' 'for him,' 'with her.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a simple preposition?

options.A: A preposition formed from more than one element
options.C: A group of words functioning as a preposition

questions.explanation: A simple preposition is a one-word preposition: at, by, for, from, in, of, off, on, to, up, with.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a compound preposition?

options.B: A preposition formed from more than one element or a compound form
options.C: A group of words functioning as a preposition
options.D: A preposition followed by a clause

questions.explanation: A compound preposition is formed from more than one element or a compound form: inside, outside, within, without, underneath, throughout.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a phrase preposition?

options.B: A preposition formed from more than one element
options.C: A group of words functioning as a preposition

questions.explanation: A phrase preposition is a group of words functioning as a preposition: because of, in front of, in spite of, on behalf of, according to, due to.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In 'Before lunch,' what part of speech is 'before'?
questions.explanation: 'Before lunch' uses before as a preposition followed by a noun phrase.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In 'I had seen it before,' what part of speech is 'before'?
questions.explanation: 'I had seen it before' uses before as an adverb.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In 'before we left,' what part of speech is 'before'?
questions.explanation: 'Before we left' uses before as a conjunction followed by a clause.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Can a sentence end with a preposition?

options.B: Yes, especially in natural questions and relative clauses
options.D: Only if the preposition is compound

questions.explanation: Yes, especially in natural questions and relative clauses: 'Who are you talking to?' and 'That is the topic I told you about.' Ending with a preposition is not inherently incorrect.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is a transitive preposition?

options.A: A preposition that has an object
options.C: A preposition that ends a sentence
options.D: A preposition formed from more than one element

questions.explanation: A transitive preposition has an object: 'She is waiting for the bus.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A preposition without an expressed object is sometimes called what?

options.C: An intransitive preposition or an adverbial particle

questions.explanation: In some grammatical analyses it is called an intransitive preposition or an adverbial particle: 'Come in'; 'He went away.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — A. Basic Concepts

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'at' used for time?

options.C: For precise clock times and specific points

questions.explanation: At is used for precise clock times and specific points: at 6 o'clock, at noon, at midnight, at sunrise, at night.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'on' used for time?
questions.explanation: On is used for days and dates: on Monday, on 15 August, on my birthday, on Monday morning.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'in' used for time?

options.C: For months, years, seasons, centuries and longer periods

questions.explanation: In is used for months, years, seasons, centuries and longer periods: in July, in 2026, in winter, in the twenty-first century.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the basic difference among at, on and in for time?

options.A: At = longer period; on = day; in = precise time
options.B: At = precise time; on = day/date; in = longer period
options.C: At = day; on = precise time; in = date
options.D: All three are interchangeable for time

questions.explanation: At = precise time; on = day/date; in = longer period. Examples: at 7 p.m.; on Tuesday; in September.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'since' used?

options.B: To indicate the starting point of a period continuing up to a reference time
options.D: To indicate the endpoint of a continuing action

questions.explanation: Since indicates the starting point of a period continuing up to a reference time: since Monday, since 2020, since childhood.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'for' used for time?

options.D: To indicate a specific clock time

questions.explanation: For indicates duration: for two hours, for three days, for ten years.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'since' and 'for'?

options.C: Both are used only for duration
options.D: Both are used only for starting points

questions.explanation: Since + starting point; for + duration. 'since 8 a.m.'; 'for three hours.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'during' used?

options.C: To mean within a period or event

questions.explanation: During means within a period or event: during the meeting, during the holidays, during the night.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'during' and 'for'?

options.A: During states how long something lasts; for identifies the period/event
options.B: During identifies the period/event in which something happens; for states how long it lasts
options.D: During is used for deadlines; for is used for starting points

questions.explanation: During identifies the period/event in which something happens; for states how long it lasts: 'during the class'; 'for an hour.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'by' used for time?

options.C: To mean not later than a deadline
options.D: To indicate continuation up to a time

questions.explanation: By means not later than a deadline: 'Submit the form by Friday.' It allows completion at or before the stated time.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'until/till' used?

options.A: To indicate a deadline for completion
options.B: To indicate that a situation continues up to a time

questions.explanation: Until or till indicates that a situation continues up to a time: 'Wait until 5 p.m.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'by' and 'until'?

options.A: By gives the endpoint of a continuing action; until gives a deadline for completion
options.B: By gives a deadline for completion; until gives the endpoint of a continuing action or state
options.D: By is used for duration; until is used for starting points

questions.explanation: By gives a deadline for completion; until gives the endpoint of a continuing action or state: 'Finish by five'; 'Stay until five.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'from' used for time?

options.B: To mark the starting point, commonly with to or until
options.D: To indicate a continuing state up to a time

questions.explanation: From marks the starting point, commonly with to or until: 'The office is open from 9 to 5.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'within' used for time?

options.A: To mean after the end of a specified period
options.B: To mean before the end of a specified period
options.D: To indicate a deadline for completion only

questions.explanation: Within means before the end of a specified period: 'Reply within two days.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'before' used?

options.A: To mean earlier than a time or event
options.B: To mean later than a time or event

questions.explanation: Before means earlier than a time or event: 'before lunch,' 'before 6 p.m.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'after' used?

options.A: To mean earlier than a time or event
options.B: To mean later than a time or event

questions.explanation: After means later than a time or event: 'after dinner,' 'after the examination.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'past' used with clock time?

options.A: To indicate minutes remaining before the next hour
options.B: To indicate minutes after an hour

questions.explanation: Past indicates minutes after an hour: ten past six = 6:10.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'to' used with clock time?

options.A: To indicate minutes after an hour
options.B: To indicate minutes remaining before the next hour

questions.explanation: To indicates minutes remaining before the next hour: ten to six = 5:50.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which preposition is commonly used in the phrase 'at the weekend'?

options.A: At the weekend is common in British English; on the weekend is common in American English
options.B: In the weekend is common in British English
options.C: On the weekend is common in British English; at the weekend is common in American English
options.D: By the weekend is the standard form

questions.explanation: At the weekend is common in British English; on the weekend is common in American English.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which preposition is used in the phrases 'in the morning,' 'in the afternoon' and 'in the evening'?
questions.explanation: In: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening. The fixed expression is at night.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the fixed expression for 'night'?
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is at night.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Is a preposition used before next, last, this and every in time expressions?
questions.explanation: Normally no: next Monday, last year, this evening, every morning—not 'on next Monday' or 'in last year.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — B. Prepositions of Time

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'at' used for place?

options.A: To indicate being inside an enclosed space
options.B: To identify a point or location
options.C: To indicate contact with a surface
options.D: To indicate movement towards a destination

questions.explanation: At identifies a point or location: at the bus stop, at the entrance, at the airport, at home.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'in' used for place?

options.A: To identify a point or location
options.B: To indicate contact with a surface
options.C: To indicate being inside an enclosed space or within an area
options.D: To indicate movement to a surface

questions.explanation: In indicates being inside an enclosed space or within an area: in the room, in a box, in Bengaluru, in India.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'on' used for place?

options.A: To indicate contact with or position on a surface
options.B: To indicate being inside an enclosed space
options.C: To identify a point or location
options.D: To indicate movement from outside to inside

questions.explanation: On indicates contact with or position on a surface: on the table, on the wall, on the floor.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between at, in and on for place?

options.A: At = inside; in = on a surface; on = a point
options.B: At = a point/location; in = inside or within an area; on = on a surface
options.C: At = on a surface; in = a point; on = inside
options.D: All three are interchangeable for place

questions.explanation: At = a point/location; in = inside or within an area; on = on a surface. Context can affect the choice.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'under' used?

options.A: To mean at a lower level than something, not necessarily directly beneath it
options.B: To mean directly or generally below something
options.C: To mean at a higher level than something

questions.explanation: Under means directly or generally below something: 'The shoes are under the bed.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'below' used?

options.B: To mean at a lower level than something, not necessarily directly beneath it
options.C: To mean at a higher level than something

questions.explanation: Below means at a lower level than something, not necessarily directly beneath it: 'The temperature fell below zero.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'over' used?

options.B: To mean above, covering, crossing or more than

questions.explanation: Over can mean above, covering, crossing or more than: 'A lamp hangs over the table'; 'over 100 people.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'above' used?

options.A: To mean at a higher level than something
options.B: To mean at a lower level than something

questions.explanation: Above means at a higher level than something: 'The picture is above the sofa.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'over' and 'above'?

options.A: Over generally indicates a higher level; above often suggests covering or crossing
options.B: Both can mean higher than. Over often suggests covering, movement across or directly higher; above generally indicates a higher level or position
options.C: Over means lower than; above means higher than

questions.explanation: Both can mean higher than. Over often suggests covering, movement across or directly higher; above generally indicates a higher level or position. Usage overlaps.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'between' used?

options.A: For someone or something in a group or collective
options.B: For distinct, separate persons or things, commonly two but also more than two when individual relationships are specified
options.D: For movement from one side to another

questions.explanation: Between is used for distinct, separate persons or things, commonly two but also more than two when individual relationships are specified: 'between Ravi and Sita'; 'an agreement between the five countries.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'among' used?

options.B: For someone or something in a group or collective
options.D: For movement from one side to another

questions.explanation: Among is used for someone or something in a group or collective: 'among the students,' 'among the trees.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'between' and 'among'?

options.A: Between emphasises being within a group; among emphasises distinct individual relationships
options.B: Between commonly emphasises distinct individual relationships; among emphasises being within a group
options.C: Between is only for two; among is only for more than two

questions.explanation: Between commonly emphasises distinct individual relationships; among emphasises being within a group. The simplistic rule 'between only two' is not always correct.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'beside' used?

options.C: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Beside means next to: 'She sat beside her mother.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'besides' used?

options.B: To mean in addition to or apart from
options.C: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Besides means in addition to or apart from: 'Besides English, he knows Kannada.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'beside' and 'besides'?

options.A: Beside = in addition to; besides = next to
options.B: Beside = next to; besides = in addition to

questions.explanation: Beside = next to; besides = in addition to.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'behind' used?

options.A: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Behind means at the back of: 'The garden is behind the house.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'in front of' used?

options.A: To mean at the back of
options.B: To mean before or at the forward side of something
options.C: To mean facing or on the other side

questions.explanation: In front of means before or at the forward side of something: 'The bus stopped in front of the school.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'opposite' used?

options.C: To indicate facing or on the other side
options.D: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Opposite indicates facing or on the other side: 'The bank is opposite the post office.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'near' used?

options.D: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Near means close to: 'The station is near my house.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'next to' used?

options.D: To mean at the back of

questions.explanation: Next to means immediately beside: 'The pharmacy is next to the clinic.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'inside/outside' used?

options.A: Inside means beyond; outside means within
options.B: Inside means within; outside means beyond or not within

questions.explanation: Inside means within; outside means beyond or not within: 'inside the room'; 'outside the gate.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'within' used for place?

options.A: To mean beyond the boundaries of an area
options.B: To mean inside the boundaries or limits of an area
options.C: To mean next to an area

questions.explanation: Within means inside the boundaries or limits of an area: 'within the city limits.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — C. Prepositions of Place and Position

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'to' used?

options.A: To indicate direction, not necessarily arrival
options.B: To indicate movement towards a destination
options.C: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.D: To indicate movement to a surface

questions.explanation: To indicates movement towards a destination: 'She went to school'; 'They travelled to Mysuru.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'towards' used?

options.B: To indicate direction, not necessarily arrival
options.C: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.D: To indicate movement to a surface

questions.explanation: Towards indicates direction, not necessarily arrival: 'He walked towards the station.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'to' and 'towards'?

options.A: To marks direction without arrival; towards marks a destination reached
options.B: To commonly marks a destination reached or intended; towards marks direction and does not guarantee arrival
options.D: Both always indicate direction without arrival

questions.explanation: To commonly marks a destination reached or intended; towards marks direction and does not guarantee arrival.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'into' used?

options.B: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.C: To indicate movement to a surface
options.D: To indicate movement away from a surface

questions.explanation: Into indicates movement from outside to inside: 'The child ran into the room.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'in' used instead of 'into'?

options.A: In generally describes movement into an interior
options.B: In generally describes location, not movement into an interior
options.C: In is used only with verbs of motion
options.D: In is never used for place

questions.explanation: In generally describes location, not movement into an interior: 'She is in the room.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'onto' used?

options.A: To indicate position on a surface
options.B: To indicate movement to a surface
options.C: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.D: To indicate movement away from a surface

questions.explanation: Onto indicates movement to a surface: 'The cat jumped onto the table.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'on' and 'onto'?

options.A: On indicates movement to a surface; onto indicates position
options.B: On usually indicates position; onto indicates movement to a surface
options.C: Both indicate movement to a surface

questions.explanation: On usually indicates position; onto indicates movement to a surface: 'The book is on the desk'; 'Put it onto the desk.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'out of' used?

options.A: To indicate movement from inside to outside
options.B: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.C: To indicate movement to a surface
options.D: To indicate movement away from a surface

questions.explanation: Out of indicates movement from inside to outside: 'He came out of the house.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'off' used for movement?

options.A: To indicate movement to a surface
options.B: To indicate movement away from a surface
options.C: To indicate movement from outside to inside
options.D: To indicate movement following a line

questions.explanation: Off indicates movement away from a surface: 'The cup fell off the table.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'from' used for movement?

options.B: To indicate the starting point or source
options.C: To indicate movement to a surface
options.D: To indicate movement within an enclosed space

questions.explanation: From indicates the starting point or source: 'She came from Delhi.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'across' used?

options.A: To indicate movement within an enclosed space
options.B: To indicate movement from one side to another over a surface or open area
options.C: To indicate movement following a line
options.D: To indicate movement to a higher position

questions.explanation: Across indicates movement from one side to another over a surface or open area: 'They walked across the road.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'through' used?

options.A: To indicate movement from one side to another over a surface
options.B: To indicate movement within and from one end or side to another of an enclosed or surrounding space
options.C: To indicate movement following a line
options.D: To indicate movement to a surface

questions.explanation: Through indicates movement within and from one end or side to another of an enclosed or surrounding space: 'The train passed through a tunnel.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'across' and 'through'?

options.A: Across means within or inside something from entry to exit; through means from one side to another over a surface
options.B: Across usually means from one side to another over a surface/open area; through means within or inside something from entry to exit
options.D: Across is used for tunnels; through is used for roads

questions.explanation: Across usually means from one side to another over a surface/open area; through means within or inside something from entry to exit.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'along' used?

options.A: To indicate movement following the length or line of something
options.B: To indicate movement from one side to another
options.C: To indicate movement within an enclosed space
options.D: To indicate movement to a higher position

questions.explanation: Along indicates movement following the length or line of something: 'They walked along the river.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'past' used for movement?

options.A: To indicate moving by or beyond a point
options.B: To indicate movement following a line
options.C: To indicate movement to a surface
options.D: To indicate movement to a lower position

questions.explanation: Past means moving by or beyond a point: 'Walk past the bank and turn left.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'around' used?

options.A: To indicate movement following a straight line
options.B: To mean following a curved route, surrounding or moving in different parts of an area
options.C: To indicate movement to a higher position
options.D: To indicate movement away from a surface

questions.explanation: Around can mean following a curved route, surrounding or moving in different parts of an area: 'They walked around the lake.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'up' used for direction?

options.A: To indicate movement to a lower position
options.B: To indicate movement to a higher position
options.C: To indicate movement following a line
options.D: To indicate movement away from a surface

questions.explanation: Up indicates movement to a higher position: 'She climbed up the hill.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — D. Prepositions of Movement and Direction

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is 'down' used for direction?

options.A: To indicate movement to a higher position
options.B: To indicate movement to a lower position
options.C: To indicate movement following a line

questions.question: What is the difference between 'despite' and 'although'?

options.A: Despite is a conjunction followed by a clause; although is a preposition followed by a noun/gerund
options.B: Despite is a preposition followed by a noun/gerund; although is a conjunction followed by a clause
options.C: Both are prepositions followed by noun phrases
options.D: Both are conjunctions followed by clauses

questions.explanation: Despite is a preposition followed by a noun/gerund: despite the rain. Although is a conjunction followed by a clause: although it rained.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — I. Important Contrasts and Exam Traps

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'because of' and 'because'?

options.A: Because of is a conjunction followed by a clause; because is a preposition phrase followed by a noun phrase
options.B: Because of is a preposition phrase followed by a noun phrase; because is a conjunction followed by a clause
options.C: Both are followed by noun phrases

questions.explanation: Because of is a preposition phrase followed by a noun phrase: because of rain. Because is a conjunction followed by a clause: because it rained.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — I. Important Contrasts and Exam Traps

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'due to' and 'owing to'?

options.A: Due to is followed by a clause; owing to is followed by a noun phrase
options.B: Both can express cause and are commonly followed by a noun phrase
options.C: Due to means 'in addition to'; owing to means 'except'
options.D: Both are used only in negative sentences

questions.explanation: Both can express cause. Due to is commonly followed by a noun phrase; owing to is also followed by a noun phrase. Formal usage preferences may vary.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — I. Important Contrasts and Exam Traps

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'except' and 'besides'?

options.A: Except adds something; besides excludes something
options.B: Except excludes something; besides adds something

questions.explanation: Except excludes something; besides adds something: 'Everyone came except Ravi'; 'Besides Ravi, Sita came too.'
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — I. Important Contrasts and Exam Traps

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'by' and 'until'?

options.A: By = continuation up to a point; until = deadline
options.B: By = deadline; until = continuation up to a point
options.D: Both mean continuation up to a point

questions.explanation: By = deadline; until = continuation up to a point.
questions.source: Prepositions.pdf — I. Important Contrasts and Exam Traps

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between 'from' and 'since'?

options.A: From marks a time starting point continuing to a later reference time; since marks a starting point and can be used for places or time
options.B: From marks a starting point and can be used for places or time; since marks a time starting point continuing to a later reference time
options.C: Both are used only for places
options.D: Both are used only for duration

questions.explanation: From marks a starting point and can be used for places or time; since marks a time starting point continuing to a later reference time.
